summary: Discovery call focused on Vela's need for an embeddings + reranking pipeline. Vela runs a semantic search product with a hybrid retrieval layer (BM25 + vector db) and wants to reduce false positives with a reranker. They are evaluating Redwood Hosted for quick tests but are interested in Dedicated or Private for throughput and data controls. Key concerns: p99 latency for retrieval + rerank, expected QPS, embedding dimensionality (currently 768), and security (SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS). Agreed next step is a POC benchmark run with 1M vectors and shared query set.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-05-05
Start: 08:42 PDT
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Omar Patel (Redwood SE), Lina Torres (Redwood Solutions); Rajiv Menon (CTO, Vela), Elena Garcia (ML), Sophie Park (Infra), Tom Wu (PM)

Summary (auto): quick discovery for embeddings + rerank POC; discuss architecture and deployment options; decide on benchmarking scope and next steps.

00:00:04 Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick intros from our side, I'm Maya - AE at Redwood, and Omar is our SE who will talk through the technical bits.
00:00:12 Rajiv Menon: Hi, Rajiv here. We're the CTO at Vela, focusing on search and analytics.
00:00:16 Elena Garcia: Elena - ML eng.
00:00:18 Sophie Park: Sophie - infra.
00:00:22 Omar Patel: Awesome. High level, Maya wanna run the context?
00:00:26 Maya Chen: Yeah, sure. Vela flagged that they want help on embeddings-based retrieval and a reranker to improve relevance. You're currently using a hybrid stack, correct? BM25 + FAISS-ish?
00:00:36 Elena Garcia: Yeah we run Lucene for BM25 and a vector DB (we're experimenting with Milvus) for ANN. We currently embed with a 768-d model, and do a simple re-score but it's not great for tricky queries.
00:00:47 Omar Patel: Got it. A common pattern we see is coarse retrieval in the vector DB, then a cross-encoder or LLM-based reranker for the final ordering. That gets better precision but adds latency and cost.
00:00:58 Tom Wu: Right, our concern is user experience - we want p99 under ~300ms for a search+rerank flow ideally. At minimum p95 under 200ms.
00:01:06 Maya Chen: That's a helpful target. Can I ask expected throughput - QPS?
00:01:10 Rajiv Menon: Peak is around 200 QPS, but typical is 40 to 60. Spiky traffic during business hours.
00:01:18 Omar Patel: 200 peak with a reranker is non-trivial. Two levers: you can use a lightweight bi-encoder for first-pass and smaller cross-encoder for top-k rerank, or offload rerank to a cheaper model and accept slightly higher latency. Also batching and caching matter.
00:01:33 Elena Garcia: For dimensionality, we're tied to 768 right now. Curious if Redwood recommends 512/1536 or sticking to ours for model compatibility.
00:01:41 Omar Patel: We support arbitrary dims. Tradeoffs: higher dim can mean better embedding quality but increases index size and ANN cost. We recommend benchmarking with your current 768; if cost is a concern we can evaluate a quantized pipeline or lower-d embeddings. Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization profiles.
00:01:58 Sophie Park: On infra - we're a regulated customer, need VPC/private deployment, KMS for keys, and SOC2 attestation. Any options there?
00:02:08 Maya Chen: Yes, Redwood Private supports VPC/on-prem installs with customer-managed KMS and audit logs. We can also run Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) inside customer VPC in some cases. We'll share our security pack.
00:02:18 Rajiv Menon: Is SOC2 complete? Who hosts the logs? We need audit logs retained for 1 year.
00:02:24 Lina Torres: We are SOC2 Type II. Audit logs can be pushed to your SIEM or stored per retention policy; we'll include those specifics in the security doc we send.
00:02:32 Tom Wu: Latency wise, what's realistic for a rerank that does 50 candidates -> cross-encoder?
00:02:38 Omar Patel: For a standard cross-encoder on a modern GPU, 50 candidates reranked can be 50-200ms depending on model size and token counts. If you use an LLM-sized reranker p99 could spike. Typical approach is top-50 dense candidates with a smaller cross-encoder optimized for inference and quantized kernels. Also continuous batching helps at higher throughput.
00:02:57 Elena Garcia: Do you integrate directly with existing vector DBs or do we need to move data?
00:03:01 Maya Chen: We integrate with common vector DBs - customers use Pinecone, Milvus, Weaviate, FAISS. You can keep your index and call Redwood for reranking or we can host the vector index in Redwood for tighter optimization (less network hop).
00:03:13 Sophie Park: We prefer keeping vectors in our VPC for compliance, so low-latency network between our vector DB and Redwood Dedicated nodes would be ideal.
00:03:20 Omar Patel: That maps well to Dedicated/Private. If you keep vectors on-prem or in your VPC, we can place Dedicated nodes in the same network to hit your throughput and control data flow.
00:03:31 Rajiv Menon: Cost - ballpark per-req cost if we do a two-stage flow? We need to compare to just increasing BM25 tuning efforts.
00:03:37 Maya Chen: We'll send a cost modeling spreadsheet. General guidance: cheap bi-encoder similarity calls are low per-call; cross-encoder reranks cost more per inference. But with caching and batching you can reduce per-query cost significantly, plus reranking only top-k. We'll include sample numbers for 200 QPS steady-state.
00:03:53 Tom Wu: We saw Pinecone's pricing - curious on Redwood's advantage.
00:03:56 Omar Patel: Redwood focuses on inference economics: kernel selection, quantization, and routing to lower-cost variants when OK. Plus Dedicated plans for predictable throughput at lower unit cost.
00:04:06 Elena Garcia: On the reranker model: we were thinking of a cross-encoder trained on our relevance labels. Can Redwood host that model?
00:04:11 Omar Patel: Yes. You can bring your model weights. We support custom model hosting; we also help with quantization and throughput tuning. For reranker we often recommend smaller cross-encoder checkpoints or distillation to keep latency down.
00:04:23 Sophie Park: Any limitations on model size in private deployments?
00:04:26 Omar Patel: Not really - depends on GPU type. Private deployments can use A100/RTX-class GPUs depending on footprint. We'll propose a config in the POC.
00:04:34 Rajiv Menon: For the POC, we want to run with our production traffic slice and a test index of 1M vectors, 768 dims, and 1000 realistic queries. Can Redwood handle that?
00:04:42 Maya Chen: Yes - typical POC. Omar will draft a benchmark plan. We'll run both Hosted trial (small) to validate functionality and Dedicated/Private benchmark for production-like latency.
00:04:51 Omar Patel: Actionable: recommend test harness (1M vectors, 768-d, measurement: topk recall, MRR, p50/p95/p99 latency for retrieval + rerank). We'll also measure cost per query.
00:05:02 Elena Garcia: Do you support hybrid search - BM25 + dense merging - and reranking with cross-encoder?
00:05:07 Omar Patel: Absolutely. Hybrid retrieval is common. You can merge BM25 and vector scores, then rerank top candidates. Important to normalize scores and tune the merge weight; we can help with that.
00:05:18 Tom Wu: For integration, is there an SDK or API?
00:05:21 Maya Chen: REST and SDKs (Python/Node). We have a route for embeddings/ search and a rerank endpoint you can call with top-k candidates for quick cross-encoder scoring.
00:05:31 Rajiv Menon: What about throughput scaling? If we hit spikes, we need autoscaling without cold start latency.
00:05:36 Omar Patel: Dedicated has configurable autoscaling and burst policies. For strict SLOs, Dedicated or Private is recommended. Hosted is great for getting started, but you'll see multi-tenant variability.
00:05:47 Elena Garcia: Any references or internal benchmarks for 200 QPS with top-50 rerank?
00:05:52 Omar Patel: We have internal perf profiles; I'll attach an anonymized perf spreadsheet. Real numbers vary by model and token lengths. For example, a quantized cross-encoder on T4-class hardware can do ~150-300 reranks/sec depending on batch. But we'll run your exact benchmark.
00:06:06 Sophie Park: Security again - SAML SSO, RBAC, KMS integration - need examples of enterprise contract and data residency.
00:06:14 Maya Chen: We'll include the enterprise security packet and SSO setup guide. We support SAML/Okta, RBAC at an org level, and customer-managed KMS for Private.
00:06:23 Rajiv Menon: Who from Redwood will be our point of contact for the POC?
00:06:26 Maya Chen: I'll own the account and coordinate, Omar will lead the POC technical work. Lina will be on touchpoints for ops.
00:06:31 Tom Wu: Cool. Schedule - we want to start POC next week if possible.
00:06:35 Maya Chen: Omar, can you run the POC kickoff Thurs or Fri?
00:06:38 Omar Patel: I can do Friday morning PST. I'll send a calendar invite.
00:06:42 Elena Garcia: One more question - embeddings dimensionality. If we want reduced dims (say 512) to save space, is there a recommended approach?
00:06:49 Omar Patel: You can either train a smaller embedder or use PCA/post-processing to compress. Some customers re-embed with smaller models; others quantize. We'll include recommendations after seeing sample evals.
00:07:00 Rajiv Menon: What's the data flow if we keep vectors in our VPC but use Redwood Hosted rerank? Network egress and latency?
00:07:07 Omar Patel: That would add network hops and egress. For compliance and latency, Dedicated/Private with colocated nodes is usually preferred. Hosted is fine for dev/test but not ideal for sensitive vectors in a customer VPC.
00:07:18 Sophie Park: Ok that aligns with our preference.
00:07:21 Maya Chen: Recap / next steps: 1) Maya send pricing + perf sheet by 5/7. 2) Omar to share benchmark plan and schedule POC kickoff Friday. 3) Vela share sample queries and index snapshot. 4) Redwood to share security pack and SOC2 docs.
00:07:36 Rajiv Menon: Sounds good.
00:07:38 Tom Wu: Thanks, talk soon.
00:07:40 Maya Chen: Thanks everyone.
00:07:44 [call ends]
